blocks.text:
name: Static gates
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 8
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1538: the publish dry-run below rehearses the tag-stamped
          # stage (gh-1522), moved here from the retired nightly
          # full-quality leg — tag math needs the full tag graph
          # (blobless per gh-1477, same incantation that leg used).
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get

      # Issue #1234: the ≤2800-line file guard MOVED into crap4dart's loc
      # gate (crap4dart.yaml, wc -l parity verified by the maintainer
      # recipe in the issue) — enforced whole-tree by the
      # `crap4dart check --baseline` Quality-gates step below. The shell
      # find-exec guard (gh-1232 AC2) is gone: one enforcement point, no
      # drifted exclusions.

      # Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +
      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed a build containing /app/ (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 2: no base tag to patch.
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          echo '<html></html>' > "$d/build/index.html"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad2.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an unpatchable base tag (AC1 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 3: a missing touchpoint file.
          rm "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad3.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an incomplete build (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # fa1.dev parity pin: both web builds must keep the identical
          # release flags AND the same pinned SDK — the bundle's only edit
          # stays the base tag. (#1431): the SDK pin must be an EXACT
          # 3.47.x patch (no wildcard) — a floating patch re-resolves a new
          # engine build and moves the canvaskit/skwasm rev-hash dir the
          # size gates track.
          for wf in .github/workflows/pages.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml; do
            grep -q -- '--release' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost the --release web flag (#1100 parity)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q -- '--base-href /app/' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost --base-href /app/ (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
            grep -Eq "flutter-version: '3\.47\.[0-9]+'" "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf unpinned Flutter SDK (#1100 parity + #1431 exact-patch rule, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
          done

      # Issue #433 AC1: README CRAP badge must equal the crap4dart.yaml
      # threshold (they drifted to 8.0-vs-12.0 once). Pure python — runs on
      # every PR, including docs-only ones (a README edit is exactly the
      # drift vector).
      - name: CRAP badge/config sync guard
        run: python3 scripts/check_crap_guards.py

      # gh-1476 AC5 (PR #1479 owner directive): the GEO layer is built at
      # deploy time — gitignored, never committed, nothing to drift
      # against. So the gate builds to a temp dir and validates the
      # OUTPUT: test/site/* (no-JS crawl, robots contract, sitemap
      # integrity, JSON-LD, llms guards) serve the temp tree over loopback
      # HTTP via FA_SITE_ROOT. Stronger than the old `--check` drift gate:
      # it tests the builder itself, and hand-edited generated HTML is
      # uncommittable by construction.
      - name: GEO site build + validation (gh-1476 AC5)
        run: |
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          # The builder's post input is the site/blog/posts COPY of the
          # canonical blog/posts — keep them pinned together so the gate
          # can never validate a stale or hand-edited copy (gh-1476
          # review). PRE-sync diff: an in-place edit of the copy is red
          # (the deploy's build_blog would silently discard it). Sync,
          # then POST-sync diff: a new or edited canonical post that was
          # never copied into site/blog/posts is red.
          git diff --exit-code -- site/blog/posts site/blog/posts.json
          dart scripts/build_blog.dart
          git diff --exit-code -- site/blog/posts site/blog/posts.json
          dart scripts/build_site.dart --out "$d/site"
          FA_SITE_ROOT="$d/site" dart test test/site/

      # gh-1199 AC2: the deterministic-gate boundary is self-enforcing —
      # an integration-tagged test that looks live (real provider URL, or
      # a credential-key literal with no mock/loopback in sight) without
      # the `llm` tag fails the gate. Runs on every PR: a PR adding a live
      # test (E1) is exactly the diff this must catch.
      - name: LLM tag boundary lint (gh-1199 AC2)
        run: python3 scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py

          # generation, staged-version desync, cap trim) must redden the

          # with broken imports (the staging filter pruned lib/src/memory;
          # imports of fork-only dart_tui symbols) that only a consumer's
          # `dart analyze` ever surfaced (issue #613). Errors fail the
          # gate; warnings/infos pass, matching the static analyze stage.

          (cd /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage && dart pub publish --dry-run --ignore-warnings)

name: CRAP + duplication
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes, test-core]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 6
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared/app changes — guards green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      # Same scope gate as every other step here: on a skipped (app-only)
      # PR no dart SDK is set up, so an unconditional pub get dies with 127.
      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          pattern: coverage-shard-*
          path: coverage-shards

      - name: Merge shard coverage (union DA hits per file, NOT cat)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          mkdir -p coverage
          python3 scripts/merge_lcov.py -o coverage/lcov.info coverage-shards/*/lcov.info

      - name: CRAP ratchet (threshold pinned in crap4dart.yaml)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          # Issue #447: 0.9.5+ carries the gate framework (broken_goldens
          # et al.); 0.2.1 knew only the CRAP ratchet. Both configs set
          # coverage.run_tests: false — the merged shard lcov above is the
          # coverage source; gates must not re-run the suite.
          # gh-1061: >=0.10.0 — analyzer 7.3→14.4 refresh + the
          # duplication.sources key (native cross-module scan).
          # gh-1106: >=0.11.0 — Type-2 renamed-clone detection
          # (duplication.ignore_locals) + gate baselines; the
          # duplication gate config throws on older parsers (unknown
          # keys are a ConfigException).
          # Bounded (rework review): a floating >= would auto-adopt
          # 0.12.0+ with no repo change — bump the ceiling deliberately.
          dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.11.0 <0.12.0"
          dart pub global run crap4dart analyze

      - name: Quality gates (broken goldens + Type-2 duplication, issue 1106)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart pub global run crap4dart check --baseline

      # Issue #1234 rework: 0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override (a
      # gates.loc.sources key is a ConfigException — caught here on
      # 019ede65), and the package config's sources drive the CRAP census
      # too, so test/ + example/ get the SAME loc gate from the companion
      # config (crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml) — the scope the retired shell
      # guards (gh-1232) scanned there. No baseline: nothing exceeds 2800
      # today, and the ceiling itself is the point.
      - name: Loc scope gate (test/ + example/, gh-1232 whole-tree ceiling)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart pub global run crap4dart check --config crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml --only loc

      - name: Duplication guard (lib/ < 1%)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          npx --yes jscpd@5 --min-tokens 50 --min-lines 5 --reporters json \
            --output /tmp/jscpd-ci lib/ || true
          python3 - <<'EOF'
          import json, sys
          try:
              with open('/tmp/jscpd-ci/jscpd-report.json') as f:
                  pct = json.load(f)['statistics']['total']['percentage']
          except Exception:
              pct = 0.0
          print(f'Duplication: {pct}% (threshold < 1.0%)')
          sys.exit(0 if float(pct) < 1.0 else 1)
          EOF

      # Issue #487: cross-module duplication gate (issue body measured 20
      # files shipped as app↔core/fa_ui/browser_ext clones). Runs the SAME
      # stage the pre-commit hook runs — one marker, parity diffable. The
      # app leg matters: most cross-module clones are born on the app side
      # and the CRAP/dup steps above stay core/shared-scoped.
      - name: Cross-module duplication ratchet (issue #487)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true'
        run: scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --stages dupx

      # The timing numbers land in the job log; the bounds assertions

      - name: Windowed-open scale evidence (issue #135 AC1)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          dart run scripts/gen_session_fixture.dart \
            --records 100000 --out /tmp/big-session.jsonl \
            --branches 3 --images --compactions --measure | tee /tmp/ac1.log

## PR Description

Closes #1679
### What changed
Provider-key persistence failures are now loud at the moment they happen (gh-1679): the add/edit-provider wizard consumes the `SecureKeyCache.save` boolean it previously swallowed and prints a `/key set`-parity failure line (slot + store label + diagnostic, never the value); the recorded entry carries a persisted `keyNotPersisted` marker so the next boot prints one degradation line per affected slot with the retry command; the no-key skip reason / 401 hint renders a distinct "secure store not writable" state via `HostKeyResolver` (`storeDegraded`/`lastStoreError`) and `KeyStatusRenderer`; a missing macOS default keychain prints an advisory remedy (text only) and offers the repair as an explicit `[y/N]` step that re-attempts the save on `y`.

### Key decisions
- `SecureKeyCache` tracks failed-save NAMES with per-name diagnostics (success clears a name); the gh-1059 `saveFailures`/`lastSaveError` counters stay unchanged for `/key` status.
- Cross-boot degradation rides the existing config persistence: a `keyNotPersisted: true` yaml field on `CustomProviderEntry` (absent when false — existing configs stay byte-identical); the boot note skips entries whose slot has since resolved.
- Key resolution order untouched; golden gh-1570 / gh-1226 / gh-1000 fixtures pass unmodified. AC7's repair runs `security default-keychain -s …` only on an explicit `y`, through the injectable `ExecutionEnv`.
- Second-tier items not in this card's core (env-provenance banner, pick-time masked prompt, `/key import-env`) were left out; wizard ⇄ `/key set` failure handling converges on the shared `could not save <slot> to <label>: the write failed` surface (locked by a parity test).

```bash
dart test test/secrets/secure_key_save_degradation_test.dart \

  test/cli/secure_key_save_degradation_boot_test.dart \

dart analyze lib bin

# gh-1679: [GOAL] Provider-key persistence must be loud: wizard save failures surface on the spot (kimi_ira 401 "no key set" RCA — silent SecureKeyCache.save swallow)

## Description

## Incident & RCA (v2 — supersedes the env-provenance framing of the first revision)

**Symptom.** On a host with two same-endpoint custom providers (`kimi_me`, `kimi_ira`, both `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`), every new session that picks `kimi_ira` fails at the first request with:

```
error: 401: Invalid Authentication — no key set; store one with /key set FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA <value>
```

The user pasted the key via the CLI add/edit-provider wizard; the provider worked in that session; the key is "gone" in the next session. Reproducible by starting a new `fa` session and selecting `kimi_ira` in the model picker.

### Live evidence (2026-10-17, host of record, fa 1.0.596)

1. **Keychain reads work; the slot set is real.** macOS Keychain (service `fah`) holds `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_ME`, `FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI`, `FA_KEY_GATE_JOINGONKA_AI_JOINGONKA`, `FA_KEY_API_AIIN_BY`, `FA_KEY_API_MINIMAX_IO_MINIMAX`. It does **not** hold `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA` nor the host-scoped `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM`.
2. **Keychain writes fail on this host right now.** A canary write (`security add-generic-password -s fah -a FA_KEY_TEST_CANARY …`, cleaned up afterwards, no residue) fails with `SecKeychainItemCreateFromContent (<default>): The authorization was canceled by the user` (exit 154) — the user canceled the system's **"reset to default"** keychain dialog.
3. **Cause of the write failure: no default keychain pointer.** `security default-keychain` → `SecKeychainCopyDefault: A default keychain could not be found` (exit 1). The search list is intact (`login.keychain-db`, System keychain) and the login keychain is unlocked (`no-timeout`) — so **reads succeed via the search list while writes fail**, because `add-generic-password` targets `<default>`, which does not resolve. (This is exactly the broken-state the fa code comments anticipate: "with no default keychain … `add-generic-password` pops the system 'Keychain Not Found' dialog before failing".)
4. **The wizard is result-blind to this failure.** `_persistSetupKey` (`lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart:415`) checks only the store preflight (`keys.available` — a `which security` probe that stays TRUE on this host) and then **ignores the boolean** `SecureKeyCache.save` returns (`lib/src/secrets/secure_key_store.dart:218` — returns `false` on any write failure, never throws). On failure it prints nothing, returns the keyName, and the entry is recorded with `keyName: FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA`. The session itself keeps working because the switch rides the freshly typed token.
5. **`/key set` handles the identical failure correctly** — `if (!await keys.save(...))` prints `could not save <NAME> to macOS Keychain: the write failed (locked or managed keychain?)`. The two write paths disagree; only the wizard path is silent.
6. **No diagnostics anywhere.** `~/.fah/logs` contains no keychain/save lines: `SecureKeyCache` only keeps in-memory counters (`saveFailures`/`lastSaveError`, collected for gh-1059 and consumed only by `/key` status), and the wizard's swallow means the failure reaches no log, no banner, no notice stream.
7. The one-shot `export FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA=…` in `~/.zsh_history` (not in any rc file) was the user's workaround for the 401s — it masked the real defect and produced the "works in one terminal, dead in another" pattern.

### Mechanism of the incident

- `kimi_me`'s key landed in the keychain while writes still worked (it predates the breakage).
- `kimi_ira`'s key, pasted in the wizard, hit a failing write (the missing default keychain — the same failure reproducible today — or a canceled ACL prompt). The wizard silently recorded the entry with its keyName; the store stayed empty; the session worked off the typed token.
- Next boot: the resolution chain (`resolveEndpointKeyName`, `lib/src/model_roles/provider_key_resolver.dart`) probes the pinned slot (empty) → host-scoped slot (empty) → no key → the skip reason / 401 hint says "no key set", which is *technically true of the durable store* and **practically a lie** from the user's viewpoint ("I pasted it, it worked, the config names the slot").

### Root cause (the fixable defect)

**The provider wizard conflates "secure store available" with "key persisted."** `SecureKeyCache.save` is designed to degrade to session-only (`false`, never throw); the wizard is the one write path that ignores the result, so a whole class of host failures (missing default keychain, locked/MDM keychain, ACL denial after a re-signed `fa update`, helper timeout) becomes a delayed, self-contradicting 401 instead of an immediate, actionable message. Secondary defects: boot never surfaces prior save degradations, and the no-key error cannot distinguish "slot empty" from "store not writable".

**Superseded framing (v1):** the first revision of this card framed the problem as env-vs-keychain provenance visibility. The env export turned out to be the workaround, not the cause. Env-provenance remains in scope as a second-tier capability (E5/AC-optional below), but the card is re-prioritized around loud persistence.

---

## Goal — provider-key persistence failures are loud at the moment they happen (v2)

**A key that did not reach the durable store can never masquerade as saved: the wizard reports a failed write on the spot, the boot banner surfaces prior save degradations, and the no-key error distinguishes "slot empty" from "store not writable".**

Today the add/edit-provider wizard, `/key set`, and the boot snapshot share one write/read chain (`SecureKeyStore`/`SecureKeyCache`), but only `/key set` consumes the write result. This card closes that gap and makes store health a first-class, always-visible property — without changing key resolution semantics.

## Architecture

No new protocols. Three changes on existing seams:

```
wizard key step ──► _persistSetupKey ──► SecureKeyCache.save ──┬─ true  → entry + key (today)
                                                               └─ false → LOUD message (NEW, parity
                                                                    with /key set) + degradation note
boot ──► SecureKeyCache (NEW: failed-save NAMES, not just count)
              └─ saveFailures > 0 → banner/notice line per name + last error + remediation
no-key skip reason / 401 hint ──► store-health state (NEW: "store not writable"
                                   vs "slot empty", naming the last diagnostic)
```

Invariants:
- Key resolution ORDER is untouched (pin → endpoint slot family → env leg on default endpoint) — gh-1570 / gh-1226 / gh-1000 golden fixtures keep passing unmodified.
- Hints and notes name **slots and diagnostics only, never values**.
- fa **detects and reports** host keychain state but never modifies system keychain settings (no auto `set-keychain`, no clicking through the system's "reset to default" remedy on the user's behalf) — the remedy is advisory text.
- The pick-time prompt and persist path keep reusing the single `/key set` write implementation.

## Capability surface

| Capability | Subject | Shape | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wizard loud save failure | the key being persisted by add/edit provider | on `save == false`: immediate message naming the slot, the store label, and the diagnostic (parity with `/key set`); the entry is still recorded but carries a visible "key not persisted" note at the next boot | core |
| Boot save-degradation note | failed save attempts since the slot last succeeded | `SecureKeyCache` tracks failed NAMES (not just a count); boot prints one line per affected slot + `lastSaveError` + the retry command | core |
| Store-health-aware no-key hint | the no-key skip reason / 401 hint | third state alongside "no key set": "secure store not writable / last write failed (diagnostic) — keys pasted earlier may not have persisted; fix the store, then `/key set <slot> <value>`" | core |
| `/key` status parity | the existing `/key` list | unchanged (already correct) — the parity TEST locks wizard ⇄ …

name: Static gates
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 8
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1538: the publish dry-run below rehearses the tag-stamped
          # stage (gh-1522), moved here from the retired nightly
          # full-quality leg — tag math needs the full tag graph
          # (blobless per gh-1477, same incantation that leg used).
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get

      # Issue #1234: the ≤2800-line file guard MOVED into crap4dart's loc
      # gate (crap4dart.yaml, wc -l parity verified by the maintainer
      # recipe in the issue) — enforced whole-tree by the
      # `crap4dart check --baseline` Quality-gates step below. The shell
      # find-exec guard (gh-1232 AC2) is gone: one enforcement point, no
      # drifted exclusions.

      # Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +
      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed a build containing /app/ (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 2: no base tag to patch.
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          echo '<html></html>' > "$d/build/index.html"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad2.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an unpatchable base tag (AC1 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 3: a missing touchpoint file.
          rm "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad3.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an incomplete build (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # fa1.dev parity pin: both web builds must keep the identical
          # release flags AND the same pinned SDK — the bundle's only edit
          # stays the base tag. (#1431): the SDK pin must be an EXACT
          # 3.47.x patch (no wildcard) — a floating patch re-resolves a new
          # engine build and moves the canvaskit/skwasm rev-hash dir the
          # size gates track.
          for wf in .github/workflows/pages.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml; do
            grep -q -- '--release' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost the --release web flag (#1100 parity)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q -- '--base-href /app/' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost --base-href /app/ (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
            grep -Eq "flutter-version: '3\.47\.[0-9]+'" "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf unpinned Flutter SDK (#1100 parity + #1431 exact-patch rule, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
          done

      # Issue #433 AC1: README CRAP badge must equal the crap4dart.yaml
      # threshold (they drifted to 8.0-vs-12.0 once). Pure python — runs on
      # every PR, including docs-only ones (a README edit is exactly the
      # drift vector).
      - name: CRAP badge/config sync guard
        run: python3 scripts/check_crap_guards.py

      # gh-1476 AC5 (PR #1479 owner directive): the GEO layer is built at
      # deploy time — gitignored, never committed, nothing to drift
      # against. So the gate builds to a temp dir and validates the
      # OUTPUT: test/site/* (no-JS crawl, robots contract, sitemap
      # integrity, JSON-LD, llms guards) serve the temp tree over loopback
      # HTTP via FA_SITE_ROOT. Stronger than the old `--check` drift gate:
      # it tests the builder itself, and hand-edited generated HTML is
      # uncommittable by construction.
      - name: GEO site build + validation (gh-1476 AC5)
        run: |
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          # The builder's post input is the site/blog/posts COPY of the
          # canonical blog/posts — keep them pinned together so the gate
          # can never validate a stale or hand-edited copy (gh-1476
          # review). PRE-sync diff: an in-place edit of the copy is red
          # (the deploy's build_blog would silently discard it). Sync,
          # then POST-sync diff: a new or edited canonical post that was
          # never copied into site/blog/posts is red.
          git diff --exit-code -- site/blog/posts site/blog/posts.json
          dart scripts/build_blog.dart
          git diff --exit-code -- site/blog/posts site/blog/posts.json
          dart scripts/build_site.dart --out "$d/site"
          FA_SITE_ROOT="$d/site" dart test test/site/

      # gh-1199 AC2: the deterministic-gate boundary is self-enforcing —
      # an integration-tagged test that looks live (real provider URL, or
      # a credential-key literal with no mock/loopback in sight) without
      # the `llm` tag fails the gate. Runs on every PR: a PR adding a live
      # test (E1) is exactly the diff this must catch.
      - name: LLM tag boundary lint (gh-1199 AC2)
        run: python3 scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py

      # gh-1199 AC6/E3: the flake quarantine list itself must stay
      # honest — every entry documented (issue, since, >=2 proving runs)
      # and pointing at an existing integration-tagged file.
      - name: Flake quarantine list guard (gh-1199 AC6)
        run: python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py --check

      # gh-1296 NG1/AC2: every lockfile in the repo is committed and
      # enforced — ONE inventory list (scripts/check_lockfiles.sh) fails the
      # PR when a listed lockfile is missing, untracked, or gitignored, and
      # the guard's own red exits are fixture-self-tested so the check
      # cannot rot silently (#1100 pattern).
      - name: Lockfile inventory gate (gh-1296 NG1)
        run: bash scripts/check_lockfiles.sh inventory

      # gh-1522 AC5: committed pubspecs carry the FIXED 0.0.0-dev
      # placeholder — the git tag is the single source of truth and CI
      # stamps the staged publish tree from it. A hand-bumped version in
      # either pubspec is a mistake now: it desyncs the tag↔staged-file
      # invariant the publish stamper relies on (and reintroduces the
      # lockfile churn gh-1522 retires). Runs on every PR — a bump attempt
      # is exactly the diff this must catch.
      - name: Version placeholder guard (gh-1522)
        run: |…

# warn band; unbudgeted shard is loud; update is down-only) so the
      # ratchet cannot rot silently (#1100 pattern).
      - name: Duration budget gate self-test (gh-1300 AC6)
        run: bash scripts/duration_budget_selftest.sh

      # gh-1364: the flake watcher's issue dedup is fixture-self-tested
      # against a stubbed gh (no network) — a tracker whose title carries
      # the `(#<digits>...` suffix GitHub search silently cannot see is
      # still found (no --search anywhere; dedup keys on the body's
      # **File**: path, not the truncated title), a create landing beside
      # an existing open tracker closes itself and fails loudly, a closed
      # tracker is re-opened instead of re-filed next to, and runs already
      # in comments are not re-commented (#1100 pattern).
      - name: Flake watcher dedup self-test (gh-1364)
        run: bash scripts/flake_watch_selftest.sh

      # gh-1568: the SM merge guard's gh-side lookups are fixture-tested
      # against the REAL commits-API shape (tree nested under `commit`)
      # on a PATH-stubbed gh — the `.tree.sha` jq bug false-alarmed every
      # merge-commit landing, and the missing conclusion field made the
      # live path alarm on every push. Covers tree/head/race/404 paths
      # and the self-diagnosing alarm body (#1100 pattern).
      - name: SM merge guard self-test (gh-1568)
        run: bash scripts/sm_merge_guard_selftest.sh

      # gh-1625: the release-event dedupe pre-check is fixture-self-tested
      # against a PATH-stubbed gh — recent/stale/no push run for the tag,
      # the 6h window boundary, non-release arms making NO API call, and
      # a failing `gh run list` degrading to dedupe=false — so the
      # release twin's short-circuit cannot rot silently before the next
      # release (#1100 pattern).
      - name: Release dedupe self-test (gh-1625)
        run: bash scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh

      # #1431: the size-budget gate's own red exits are fixture-tested
      # (#1100 pattern) — an engine rev-hash rename must UPDATE not NEW,
      # vendored engine churn warns instead of reddening, first-party
      # payload still fails hard, and the 20+hex regex leaves first-party
      # paths that merely contain hex alone.
      - name: Size manifest gate self-test (#1431)
        run: python3 scripts/test_size_manifest.py

      # Full analyze needs the example app's package config (Flutter imports);
      # a docs-only PR skips the flutter setup entirely and analyzes the pure
      # Dart scopes only — it cannot have changed resolution anyway.
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Example app setup (full analyze only)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          printf 'OPENROUTER_API_KEY=\nMODEL_ID=\nBASE_URL=\nHUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=\n' > [REDACTED:Credential File]
          cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
          dart pub get --directory=office_addin/dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
      - name: dart analyze (full)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        # pana score: infos dock points — keep zero
        run: dart analyze --fatal-infos --fatal-warnings

      - name: dart analyze (docs-only scope)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        # pana score: infos dock points — keep zero
        run: dart analyze --fatal-infos --fatal-warnings lib test bin

      # Publish gate at PR time: publish-blocking problems (undeclared lib/
      # imports, stray PEM-like strings) used to surface only in the tag-time
      # publish job — the v0.1.331 era: an undeclared package:cryptography
      # import shipped red on ~26 consecutive tags. --ignore-warnings: the
      # two known layout warnings (gitignored install_local.sh, docs/
      # naming) must not redden every PR, while validation ERRORS — "does
      # not have X in the dependencies section of pubspec.yaml" — still
      # fail. setup-dart (sdk >= 3.13) registers a publish-scoped PUB_TOKEN
      # job-wide and pub.dev rejects authenticated metadata reads, so
      # resolve unauthenticated (same pattern as the publish job);
      # --dry-run never uploads.
      - name: Publish dry-run (unauthenticated)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          dart pub token remove https://pub.dev || true
          # Against the STAGED tree, not the repo root (#597 AC1): the
          # publish job publishes from the stage — the v0.1.407 class of
          # failure (staged resolution re-pinning vendor/dart_tui through
          # pubspec_overrides.yaml) must redden the PR, not the tag.
          bash scripts/stage_publish_package.sh /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage
          # gh-1538: the STAMP rehearsal moved here from the retired nightly
          # full-quality leg — the pre-merge gate is the single test gate
          # now, so a stamp failure (placeholder leak, changelog-section
          # generation, staged-version desync, cap trim) must redden the
          # PR, not surface at tag time. Rehearses the NEXT tag's payload
          # exactly like the nightly leg did (gh-1522).
          latest=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1)
          latest="${latest#v}"
          IFS='.' read -r major minor patch <<< "$latest"
          next="$major.$minor.$((patch + 1))"
          echo "rehearsing the stamp of the NEXT tag: v$next"
          bash scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage "$next"
          # The staged tree must ANALYZE clean: v0.1.411 shipped files
          # with broken imports (the staging filter pruned lib/src/memory;
          # imports of fork-only dart_tui symbols) that only a consumer's
          # `dart analyze` ever surfaced (issue #613). Errors fail the
          # gate; warnings/infos pass, matching the static analyze stage.
          (cd /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage && dart pub get && dart analyze)
          (cd /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage && dart pub publish --dry-run --ignore-warnings)

    # Always runs (no job-level path gate): a path-filtered matrix skip
    # posts a check-run with the LITERAL unrendered name — the required
    # contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]

name: CRAP + duplication
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes, test-core]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 6
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared/app changes — guards green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      # Same scope gate as every other step here: on a skipped (app-only)
      # PR no dart SDK is set up, so an unconditional pub get dies with 127.
      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          pattern: coverage-shard-*
          path: coverage-shards

      - name: Merge shard coverage (union DA hits per file, NOT cat)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          mkdir -p coverage
          python3 scripts/merge_lcov.py -o coverage/lcov.info coverage-shards/*/lcov.info

      - name: CRAP ratchet (threshold pinned in crap4dart.yaml)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          # Issue #447: 0.9.5+ carries the gate framework (broken_goldens
          # et al.); 0.2.1 knew only the CRAP ratchet. Both configs set
          # coverage.run_tests: false — the merged shard lcov above is the
          # coverage source; gates must not re-run the suite.
          # gh-1061: >=0.10.0 — analyzer 7.3→14.4 refresh + the
          # duplication.sources key (native cross-module scan).
          # gh-1106: >=0.11.0 — Type-2 renamed-clone detection
          # (duplication.ignore_locals) + gate baselines; the
          # duplication gate config throws on older parsers (unknown
          # keys are a ConfigException).
          # Bounded (rework review): a floating >= would auto-adopt
          # 0.12.0+ with no repo change — bump the ceiling deliberately.
          dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.11.0 <0.12.0"
          dart pub global run crap4dart analyze

      - name: Quality gates (broken goldens + Type-2 duplication, issue 1106)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart pub global run crap4dart check --baseline

      # Issue #1234 rework: 0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override (a
      # gates.loc.sources key is a ConfigException — caught here on
      # 019ede65), and the package config's sources drive the CRAP census
      # too, so test/ + example/ get the SAME loc gate from the companion
      # config (crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml) — the scope the retired shell
      # guards (gh-1232) scanned there. No baseline: nothing exceeds 2800
      # today, and the ceiling itself is the point.
      - name: Loc scope gate (test/ + example/, gh-1232 whole-tree ceiling)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart pub global run crap4dart check --config crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml --only loc

      - name: Duplication guard (lib/ < 1%)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          npx --yes jscpd@5 --min-tokens 50 --min-lines 5 --reporters json \
            --output /tmp/jscpd-ci lib/ || true

          import json, sys
          try:
              with open('/tmp/jscpd-ci/jscpd-report.json') as f:
                  pct = json.load(f)['statistics']['total']['percentage']
          except Exception:
              pct = 0.0
          print(f'Duplication: {pct}% (threshold < 1.0%)')
          sys.exit(0 if float(pct) < 1.0 else 1)
          EOF

      # stage the pre-commit hook runs — one marker, parity diffable. The

        run: |
          dart run scripts/gen_session_fixture.dart \
            --records 100000 --out /tmp/big-session.jsonl \
            --branches 3 --images --compactions --measure | tee /tmp/ac1.log

## PR Description

Closes #1679
### What changed
Provider-key persistence failures are now loud at the moment they happen (gh-1679): the add/edit-provider wizard consumes the `SecureKeyCache.save` boolean it previously swallowed and prints a `/key set`-parity failure line (slot + store label + diagnostic, never the value); the recorded entry carries a persisted `keyNotPersisted` marker so the next boot prints one degradation line per affected slot with the retry command; the no-key skip reason / 401 hint renders a distinct "secure store not writable" state via `HostKeyResolver` (`storeDegraded`/`lastStoreError`) and `KeyStatusRenderer`; a missing macOS default keychain prints an advisory remedy (text only) and offers the repair as an explicit `[y/N]` step that re-attempts the save on `y`.

### Key decisions
- `SecureKeyCache` tracks failed-save NAMES with per-name diagnostics (success clears a name); the gh-1059 `saveFailures`/`lastSaveError` counters stay unchanged for `/key` status.
- Cross-boot degradation rides the existing config persistence: a `keyNotPersisted: true` yaml field on `CustomProviderEntry` (absent when false — existing configs stay byte-identical); the boot note skips entries whose slot has since resolved.
- Key resolution order untouched; golden gh-1570 / gh-1226 / gh-1000 fixtures pass unmodified. AC7's repair runs `security default-keychain -s …` only on an explicit `y`, through the injectable `ExecutionEnv`.
- Second-tier items not in this card's core (env-provenance banner, pick-time masked prompt, `/key import-env`) were left out; wizard ⇄ `/key set` failure handling converges on the shared `could not save <slot> to <label>: the write failed` surface (locked by a parity test).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/secrets/secure_key_save_degradation_test.dart \
  test/cli/provider_wizard_loud_save_test.dart \
  test/cli/secure_key_save_degradation_boot_test.dart \
  test/model_roles/provider_key_resolver_store_health_test.dart
dart analyze lib bin
```

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  W[wizard key step] --> P[_persistSetupKey]
  P -->|save true| E[entry + key, byte-identical]
  P -->|save false| L[LOUD line: slot + label + diagnostic]
  L --> D{missing default keychain?}
  D -->|yes| O["[y/N] repair offer — runs only on y, then re-saves"]
  D -->|no| F[entry recorded with keyNotPersisted flag]
  O -->|n| F
  B[boot] --> N[secureKeySaveDegradationLines]
  N -->|flagged entry, empty slot| BL["one line per slot + retry command (stderr)"]
  H[no-key hint / 401] --> S{store degraded?}
  S -->|yes| HW["secure store not writable (diagnostic) … /key set"]
  S -->|no| HP["no key set; store one with /key set"]
```

# gh-1679: [GOAL] Provider-key persistence must be loud: wizard save failures surface on the spot (kimi_ira 401 "no key set" RCA — silent SecureKeyCache.save swallow)

## Description

## Incident & RCA (v2 — supersedes the env-provenance framing of the first revision)

**Symptom.** On a host with two same-endpoint custom providers (`kimi_me`, `kimi_ira`, both `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`), every new session that picks `kimi_ira` fails at the first request with:

```
error: 401: Invalid Authentication — no key set; store one with /key set FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA <value>
```

The user pasted the key via the CLI add/edit-provider wizard; the provider worked in that session; the key is "gone" in the next session. Reproducible by starting a new `fa` session and selecting `kimi_ira` in the model picker.

### Live evidence (2026-10-17, host of record, fa 1.0.596)

1. **Keychain reads work; the slot set is real.** macOS Keychain (service `fah`) holds `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_ME`, `FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI`, `FA_KEY_GATE_JOINGONKA_AI_JOINGONKA`, `FA_KEY_API_AIIN_BY`, `FA_KEY_API_MINIMAX_IO_MINIMAX`. It does **not** hold `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA` nor the host-scoped `FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM`.
2. **Keychain writes fail on this host right now.** A canary write (`security add-generic-password -s fah -a FA_KEY_TEST_CANARY …`, cleaned up afterwards, no residue) fails with `SecKeychainItemCreateFromContent (<default>): The authorization was canceled by the user` (exit 154) — the user canceled the system's **"reset to default"** keychain dialog.
3. **Cause of the write failure: no default keychain pointer.** `security default-keychain` → `SecKeychainCopyDefault: A default keychain could not be found` (exit 1). The search list is intact (`login.keychain-db`, System keychain) and the login keychain is unlocked (`no-timeout`) — so **reads succeed via the search list while writes fail**, because `add-generic-password` targets `<default>`, which does not resolve. (This is exactly the broken-state the fa code comments anticipate: "with no default keychain … `add-generic-password` pops the system 'Keychain Not Found' dialog before failing".)
4. **The wizard is result-blind to this failure.** `_persistSetupKey` (`lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart:415`) checks only the store preflight (`keys.available` — a `which security` probe that stays TRUE on this host) and then **ignores the boolean** `SecureKeyCache.save` returns (`lib/src/secrets/secure_key_store.dart:218` — returns `false` on any write failure, never throws). On failure it prints nothing, returns the keyName, and the entry is recorded with `keyName: FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA`. The session itself keeps working because the switch rides the freshly typed token.
5. **`/key set` handles the identical failure correctly** — `if (!await keys.save(...))` prints `could not save <NAME> to macOS Keychain: the write failed (locked or managed keychain?)`. The two write paths disagree; only the wizard path is silent.
6. **No diagnostics anywhere.** `~/.fah/logs` contains no keychain/save lines: `SecureKeyCache` only keeps in-memory counters (`saveFailures`/`lastSaveError`, collected for gh-1059 and consumed only by `/key` status), and the wizard's swallow means the failure reaches no log, no banner, no notice stream.
7. The one-shot `export FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_KIMI_IRA=…` in `~/.zsh_history` (not in any rc file) was the user's workaround for the 401s — it masked the real defect and produced the "works in one terminal, dead in another" pattern.

### Mechanism of the incident

- `kimi_me`'s key landed in the keychain while writes still worked (it predates the breakage).
- `kimi_ira`'s key, pasted in the wizard, hit a failing write (the missing default keychain — the same failure reproducible today — or a canceled ACL prompt). The wizard silently recorded the entry with its keyName; the store stayed empty; the session worked off the typed token.
- Next boot: the resolution chain (`resolveEndpointKeyName`, `lib/src/model_roles/provider_key_resolver.dart`) probes the pinned slot (empty) → host-scoped slot (empty) → no key → the skip reason / 401 hint says "no key set", which is *technically true of the durable store* and **practically a lie** from the user's viewpoint ("I pasted it, it worked, the config names the slot").

### Root cause (the fixable defect)

**The provider wizard conflates "secure store available" with "key persisted."** `SecureKeyCache.save` is designed to degrade to session-only (`false`, never throw); the wizard is the one write path that ignores the result, so a whole class of host failures (missing default keychain, locked/MDM keychain, ACL denial after a re-signed `fa update`, helper timeout) becomes a delayed, self-contradicting 401 instead of an immediate, actionable message. Secondary defects: boot never surfaces prior save degradations, and the no-key error cannot distinguish "slot empty" from "store not writable".

**Superseded framing (v1):** the first revision of this card framed the problem as env-vs-keychain provenance visibility. The env export turned out to be the workaround, not the cause. Env-provenance remains in scope as a second-tier capability (E5/AC-optional below), but the card is re-prioritized around loud persistence.

---

## Goal — provider-key persistence failures are loud at the moment they happen (v2)

**A key that did not reach the durable store can never masquerade as saved: the wizard reports a failed write on the spot, the boot banner surfaces prior save degradations, and the no-key error distinguishes "slot empty" from "store not writable".**

Today the add/edit-provider wizard, `/key set`, and the boot snapshot share one write/read chain (`SecureKeyStore`/`SecureKeyCache`), but only `/key set` consumes the write result. This card closes that gap and makes store health a first-class, always-visible property — without changing key resolution semantics.

## Architecture

No new protocols. Three changes on existing seams:

```
wizard key step ──► _persistSetupKey ──► SecureKeyCache.save ──┬─ true  → entry + key (today)
                                                               └─ false → LOUD message (NEW, parity
                                                                    with /key set) + degradation note
boot ──► SecureKeyCache (NEW: failed-save NAMES, not just count)
              └─ saveFailures > 0 → banner/notice line per name + last error + remediation
no-key skip reason / 401 hint ──► store-health state (NEW: "store not writable"
                                   vs "slot empty", naming the last diagnostic)
```

Invariants:
- Key resolution ORDER is untouched (pin → endpoint slot family → env leg on default endpoint) — gh-1570 / gh-1226 / gh-1000 golden fixtures keep passing unmodified.
- Hints and notes name **slots and diagnostics only, never values**.
- fa **detects and reports** host keychain state but never modifies system keychain settings (no auto `set-keychain`, no clicking through the system's "reset to default" remedy on the user's behalf) — the remedy is advisory text.
- The pick-time prompt and persist path keep reusing the single `/key set` write implementation.

## Capability surface

| Capability | Subject | Shape | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wizard loud save failure | the key being persisted by add/edit provider | on `save == false`: immediate message naming the slot, the store label, and the diagnostic (parity with `/key set`); the entry is still recorded but carries a visible "key not persisted" note at the next boot | core |
| Boot save-degradation note | failed save attempts since the slot last succeeded | `SecureKeyCache` tracks failed NAMES (not just a count); boot prints one line per affected slot + `lastSaveError` + the retry command | core |
| Store-health-aware no-key hint | the no-key skip reason / 401 hint | third state alongside "no key set": "secure store not writable / last write failed (diagnostic) — keys pasted earlier may not have persisted; fix the store, then `/key set <slot> <value>`" | core |
| `/key` status parity | the existing `/key` list | unchanged (already correct) — the parity TEST locks wizard ⇄ …

name: Static gates
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 8
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1538: the publish dry-run below rehearses the tag-stamped
          # stage (gh-1522), moved here from the retired nightly
          # full-quality leg — tag math needs the full tag graph
          # (blobless per gh-1477, same incantation that leg used).
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get

      # Issue #1234: the ≤2800-line file guard MOVED into crap4dart's loc
      # gate (crap4dart.yaml, wc -l parity verified by the maintainer
      # recipe in the issue) — enforced whole-tree by the
      # `crap4dart check --baseline` Quality-gates step below. The shell
      # find-exec guard (gh-1232 AC2) is gone: one enforcement point, no
      # drifted exclusions.

      # Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +
      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed a build containing /app/ (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 2: no base tag to patch.
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          echo '<html></html>' > "$d/build/index.html"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad2.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an unpatchable base tag (AC1 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 3: a missing touchpoint file.
          rm "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad3.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an incomplete build (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # fa1.dev parity pin: both web builds must keep the identical
          # release flags AND the same pinned SDK — the bundle's only edit
          # stays the base tag. (#1431): the SDK pin must be an EXACT
          # 3.47.x patch (no wildcard) — a floating patch re-resolves a new
          # engine build and moves the canvaskit/skwasm rev-hash dir the
          # size gates track.
          for wf in .github/workflows/pages.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml; do
            grep -q -- '--release' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost the --release web flag (#1100 parity)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q -- '--base-href /app/' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost --base-href /app/ (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
            grep -Eq "flutter-version: '3\.47\.[0-9]+'" "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf unpinned Flutter SDK (#1100 parity + #1431 exact-patch rule, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }
          done

      # Issue #433 AC1: README CRAP badge must equal the crap4dart.yaml
      # threshold (they drifted to 8.0-vs-12.0 once). Pure python — runs on
      # every PR, including docs-only ones (a README edit is exactly the
      # drift vector).
      - name: CRAP badge/config sync guard
        run: python3 scripts/check_crap_guards.py

      # gh-1476 AC5 (PR #1479 owner directive): the GEO layer is built at
      # deploy time — gitignored, never committed, nothing to drift
      # against. So the gate builds to a temp dir and validates the
      # OUTPUT: test/site/* (no-JS crawl, robots contract, sitemap
      # integrity, JSON-LD, llms guards) serve the temp tree over loopback
      # HTTP via FA_SITE_ROOT. Stronger than the old `--check` drift gate:
      # it tests the builder itself, and hand-edited generated HTML is
      # uncommittable by construction.
      - name: GEO site build + validation (gh-1476 AC5)
        run: |
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          # The builder's post input is the site/blog/posts COPY of the
          # canonical blog/posts — keep them pinned together so the gate
          # can never validate a stale or hand-edited copy (gh-1476
          # review). PRE-sync diff: an in-place edit of the copy is red
          # (the deploy's build_blog would silently discard it). Sync,
          # then POST-sync diff: a new or edited canonical post that was
          # never copied into site/blog/posts is red.
          git diff --exit-code -- site/blog/posts site/blog/posts.json
          dart scripts/build_blog.dart
          git diff --exit-code -- site/blog/posts site/blog/posts.json
          dart scripts/build_site.dart --out "$d/site"
          FA_SITE_ROOT="$d/site" dart test test/site/

      # gh-1199 AC2: the deterministic-gate boundary is self-enforcing —
      # an integration-tagged test that looks live (real provider URL, or
      # a credential-key literal with no mock/loopback in sight) without
      # the `llm` tag fails the gate. Runs on every PR: a PR adding a live
      # test (E1) is exactly the diff this must catch.
      - name: LLM tag boundary lint (gh-1199 AC2)
        run: python3 scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py

      # gh-1199 AC6/E3: the flake quarantine list itself must stay
      # honest — every entry documented (issue, since, >=2 proving runs)
      # and pointing at an existing integration-tagged file.
      - name: Flake quarantine list guard (gh-1199 AC6)
        run: python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py --check

      # gh-1296 NG1/AC2: every lockfile in the repo is committed and
      # enforced — ONE inventory list (scripts/check_lockfiles.sh) fails the
      # PR when a listed lockfile is missing, untracked, or gitignored, and
      # the guard's own red exits are fixture-self-tested so the check
      # cannot rot silently (#1100 pattern).
      - name: Lockfile inventory gate (gh-1296 NG1)
        run: bash scripts/check_lockfiles.sh inventory

      # gh-1522 AC5: committed pubspecs carry the FIXED 0.0.0-dev
      # placeholder — the git tag is the single source of truth and CI
      # stamps the staged publish tree from it. A hand-bumped version in
      # either pubspec is a mistake now: it desyncs the tag↔staged-file
      # invariant the publish stamper relies on (and reintroduces the
      # lockfile churn gh-1522 retires). Runs on every PR — a bump attempt
      # is exactly the diff this must catch.
      - name: Version placeholder guard (gh-1522)
        run: |…

# warn band; unbudgeted shard is loud; update is down-only) so the
      # ratchet cannot rot silently (#1100 pattern).
      - name: Duration budget gate self-test (gh-1300 AC6)
        run: bash scripts/duration_budget_selftest.sh

      # gh-1364: the flake watcher's issue dedup is fixture-self-tested
      # against a stubbed gh (no network) — a tracker whose title carries
      # the `(#<digits>...` suffix GitHub search silently cannot see is
      # still found (no --search anywhere; dedup keys on the body's
      # **File**: path, not the truncated title), a create landing beside
      # an existing open tracker closes itself and fails loudly, a closed
      # tracker is re-opened instead of re-filed next to, and runs already
      # in comments are not re-commented (#1100 pattern).
      - name: Flake watcher dedup self-test (gh-1364)
        run: bash scripts/flake_watch_selftest.sh

      # gh-1568: the SM merge guard's gh-side lookups are fixture-tested
      # against the REAL commits-API shape (tree nested under `commit`)
      # on a PATH-stubbed gh — the `.tree.sha` jq bug false-alarmed every
      # merge-commit landing, and the missing conclusion field made the
      # live path alarm on every push. Covers tree/head/race/404 paths
      # and the self-diagnosing alarm body (#1100 pattern).
      - name: SM merge guard self-test (gh-1568)
        run: bash scripts/sm_merge_guard_selftest.sh

      # gh-1625: the release-event dedupe pre-check is fixture-self-tested
      # against a PATH-stubbed gh — recent/stale/no push run for the tag,
      # the 6h window boundary, non-release arms making NO API call, and
      # a failing `gh run list` degrading to dedupe=false — so the
      # release twin's short-circuit cannot rot silently before the next
      # release (#1100 pattern).
      - name: Release dedupe self-test (gh-1625)
        run: bash scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh

      # #1431: the size-budget gate's own red exits are fixture-tested
      # (#1100 pattern) — an engine rev-hash rename must UPDATE not NEW,
      # vendored engine churn warns instead of reddening, first-party
      # payload still fails hard, and the 20+hex regex leaves first-party
      # paths that merely contain hex alone.
      - name: Size manifest gate self-test (#1431)
        run: python3 scripts/test_size_manifest.py

      # Full analyze needs the example app's package config (Flutter imports);
      # a docs-only PR skips the flutter setup entirely and analyzes the pure
      # Dart scopes only — it cannot have changed resolution anyway.
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Example app setup (full analyze only)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          printf 'OPENROUTER_API_KEY=\nMODEL_ID=\nBASE_URL=\nHUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=\n' > [REDACTED:Credential File]
          cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
          dart pub get --directory=office_addin/dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
      - name: dart analyze (full)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        # pana score: infos dock points — keep zero
        run: dart analyze --fatal-infos --fatal-warnings

      - name: dart analyze (docs-only scope)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        # pana score: infos dock points — keep zero
        run: dart analyze --fatal-infos --fatal-warnings lib test bin

      # Publish gate at PR time: publish-blocking problems (undeclared lib/
      # imports, stray PEM-like strings) used to surface only in the tag-time
      # publish job — the v0.1.331 era: an undeclared package:cryptography
      # import shipped red on ~26 consecutive tags. --ignore-warnings: the
      # two known layout warnings (gitignored install_local.sh, docs/
      # naming) must not redden every PR, while validation ERRORS — "does
      # not have X in the dependencies section of pubspec.yaml" — still
      # fail. setup-dart (sdk >= 3.13) registers a publish-scoped PUB_TOKEN
      # job-wide and pub.dev rejects authenticated metadata reads, so
      # resolve unauthenticated (same pattern as the publish job);
      # --dry-run never uploads.
      - name: Publish dry-run (unauthenticated)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          dart pub token remove https://pub.dev || true
          # Against the STAGED tree, not the repo root (#597 AC1): the
          # publish job publishes from the stage — the v0.1.407 class of
          # failure (staged resolution re-pinning vendor/dart_tui through
          # pubspec_overrides.yaml) must redden the PR, not the tag.
          bash scripts/stage_publish_package.sh /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage
          # gh-1538: the STAMP rehearsal moved here from the retired nightly
          # full-quality leg — the pre-merge gate is the single test gate
          # now, so a stamp failure (placeholder leak, changelog-section
          # generation, staged-version desync, cap trim) must redden the
          # PR, not surface at tag time. Rehearses the NEXT tag's payload
          # exactly like the nightly leg did (gh-1522).
          latest=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1)
          latest="${latest#v}"
          IFS='.' read -r major minor patch <<< "$latest"
          next="$major.$minor.$((patch + 1))"
          echo "rehearsing the stamp of the NEXT tag: v$next"
          bash scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage "$next"
          # The staged tree must ANALYZE clean: v0.1.411 shipped files
          # with broken imports (the staging filter pruned lib/src/memory;
          # imports of fork-only dart_tui symbols) that only a consumer's
          # `dart analyze` ever surfaced (issue #613). Errors fail the
          # gate; warnings/infos pass, matching the static analyze stage.
          (cd /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage && dart pub get && dart analyze)
          (cd /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage && dart pub publish --dry-run --ignore-warnings)

  test-core:
    # Always runs (no job-level path gate): a path-filtered matrix skip
    # posts a check-run with the LITERAL unrendered name — the required
    # contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below

    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)

    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]

    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.

name: CRAP + duplication
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes, test-core]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 6
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared/app changes — guards green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      # Same scope gate as every other step here: on a skipped (app-only)
      # PR no dart SDK is set up, so an unconditional pub get dies with 127.
      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          pattern: coverage-shard-*
          path: coverage-shards

      - name: Merge shard coverage (union DA hits per file, NOT cat)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          mkdir -p coverage
          python3 scripts/merge_lcov.py -o coverage/lcov.info coverage-shards/*/lcov.info

      - name: CRAP ratchet (threshold pinned in crap4dart.yaml)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          # Issue #447: 0.9.5+ carries the gate framework (broken_goldens
          # et al.); 0.2.1 knew only the CRAP ratchet. Both configs set
          # coverage.run_tests: false — the merged shard lcov above is the
          # coverage source; gates must not re-run the suite.
          # gh-1061: >=0.10.0 — analyzer 7.3→14.4 refresh + the
          # duplication.sources key (native cross-module scan).
          # gh-1106: >=0.11.0 — Type-2 renamed-clone detection
          # (duplication.ignore_locals) + gate baselines; the
          # duplication gate config throws on older parsers (unknown
          # keys are a ConfigException).
          # Bounded (rework review): a floating >= would auto-adopt
          # 0.12.0+ with no repo change — bump the ceiling deliberately.
          dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.11.0 <0.12.0"
          dart pub global run crap4dart analyze

      - name: Quality gates (broken goldens + Type-2 duplication, issue 1106)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart pub global run crap4dart check --baseline

      # Issue #1234 rework: 0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override (a
      # gates.loc.sources key is a ConfigException — caught here on
      # 019ede65), and the package config's sources drive the CRAP census
      # too, so test/ + example/ get the SAME loc gate from the companion
      # config (crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml) — the scope the retired shell
      # guards (gh-1232) scanned there. No baseline: nothing exceeds 2800
      # today, and the ceiling itself is the point.
      - name: Loc scope gate (test/ + example/, gh-1232 whole-tree ceiling)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart pub global run crap4dart check --config crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml --only loc

      - name: Duplication guard (lib/ < 1%)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          npx --yes jscpd@5 --min-tokens 50 --min-lines 5 --reporters json \
            --output /tmp/jscpd-ci lib/ || true
          python3 - <<'EOF'
          import json, sys
          try:
              with open('/tmp/jscpd-ci/jscpd-report.json') as f:
                  pct = json.load(f)['statistics']['total']['percentage']
          except Exception:
              pct = 0.0
          print(f'Duplication: {pct}% (threshold < 1.0%)')
          sys.exit(0 if float(pct) < 1.0 else 1)
          EOF

      # Issue #487: cross-module duplication gate (issue body measured 20
      # files shipped as app↔core/fa_ui/browser_ext clones). Runs the SAME
      # stage the pre-commit hook runs — one marker, parity diffable. The
      # app leg matters: most cross-module clones are born on the app side
      # and the CRAP/dup steps above stay core/shared-scoped.
      - name: Cross-module duplication ratchet (issue #487)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true'
        run: scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --stages dupx
